items.stem: What characterises an indirect prompt-injection attack?

options.text: Malicious instructions are hidden in content the model later retrieves or reads
options.rationale: Correct: indirect injection plants instructions in data the model ingests, not the user's direct message.

options.text: The attacker guesses the model's weights
options.rationale: Weight guessing is not prompt injection.

options.text: The model runs out of memory
options.rationale: Resource exhaustion is a different class of issue.

options.text: The user asks a factual question
options.rationale: A normal question is not an injection attack.

items.explanation: Correct: indirect injection plants instructions in data the model ingests, not the user's direct message.

items.stem: Which TWO controls best reduce the impact of a successful prompt injection in a tool-using agent? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Grant each tool only the least privilege it needs
options.rationale: Correct: least privilege limits what a hijacked agent can do.

options.text: Require confirmation or filtering before high-impact actions
options.rationale: Correct: gating risky actions blocks injected commands from executing freely.

options.text: Place all secrets directly in the system prompt
options.rationale: That increases leakage risk rather than reducing injection impact.

options.text: Trust any instruction found in retrieved documents
options.rationale: Trusting untrusted data is the root of indirect injection.

items.explanation: Correct: least privilege limits what a hijacked agent can do.

items.stem: Why is a well-written system prompt insufficient on its own to stop jailbreaks?

options.text: Models can be steered by adversarial inputs that override prompt instructions
options.rationale: Correct: prompt-level defences are probabilistic and can be bypassed, so layered controls are needed.

options.text: System prompts are never sent to the model
options.rationale: They are sent; the issue is they are not a hard guarantee.

options.text: A system prompt makes the model deterministic
options.rationale: It does not guarantee determinism or safety.

items.explanation: Correct: prompt-level defences are probabilistic and can be bypassed, so layered controls are needed.
